newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Great Central jumps on Barrick bid talk.
newsitem.headline: Great Central jumps on Barrick bid talk.

text.p: Shares in gold miner Great Central Mines Ltd surged as much as 27 cents or 11 percent in active early trade on Wednesday after reports that Canada's Barrick Gold Corp was about to launch a takeover bid.

Great Central was up 19 cents at A$2.65 by 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT), having earlier risen to A$2.73 after The Australian Financial Review reported that Barrick executives had returned to Canada to polish details of the bid after a recent visit to Australia. Barrick would not comment on the speculation.

Brokers said the savage selloff in Australian gold shares in the wake of the Reserve Bank's announcement almost two weeks ago of the sale of two-thirds of its gold had put several gold producers into takeover territory.

"We've heard it spread around the market like everybody else and I think it's really the reason for the price rise today," Eyres Reed broker Martin Angel said of the Barrick-Great Central takeover speculation.
"I think there's a good chance that it could be happening," he said.
"You will find a lot of those rumours start to surface now obviously because of the gold price," said D.J. Carmichael and Co broker, Peter Saunders.
Others mentioned as possible takeover targets included Wiluna Mines Ltd and Normandy Mining Ltd, although opinion was divided about Normandy.
Brokers said the higher cost producers were the most vulnerable.
"Something like Wiluna perhaps is a possibility because it's under a bit of pressure on its costs," Angel said.
Wiluna's shares were unchanged at 35 cents at 11.00 a.m. (0100 GMT), while Normandy's shares were down one cent at A$1.50.
Overall the gold index was up 19.1 points or 1.50 percent at 1,295.8, largely due to Great Central's rise, against the overall market's 0.47 percent rise.
